reason: This passage (Ezekiel 37, the Valley of Dry Bones vision) features primarily divine action and prophetic command rather than regular people with agency. Ezekiel, while human, acts strictly under direct divine command (he prophesies as commanded), not through autonomous agency. The House of Israel is mentioned but portrayed entirely as passive objects of divine restoration—they are the 'bones' being acted upon. Their only direct speech expresses their hopelessness and lack of agency ('Our bones have dried up and our hope is lost'). Even their resurrection is entirely dependent on God's spirit/breath filling them, not on their own will or action.
